correctness.rationale: The three stationary pair-correlation equations (1) are exact consequences of the eight-state heat-bath generator; their explicitly inverted solution has denominator Δ>25 on 0<t_i<1. The current from each reservoir is the expected flip energy change, and direct substitution yields pair conductances 2J(4+t_k)/Δ>0 with exact conservation. The middle-bath zero-current mean is a strict convex combination of the other two parameters; stationarity entropy production is a nonnegative sum of products of equal-order inverse-temperature differences. The one-hot/two-hot current ratio follows from factorizations of Δ and has derivative ∂_x R=−2(8−2y−y²)/(8−xy−2y)²<0; its sharp unattained supremum 4/3 is reached only in the stated limit. Direct independent exact-rational eight-state stationary solutions agree for 125 triples. No limiting conclusion is inferred merely from finite tests.

value.rationale: The problem concerns the physically natural smallest non-bipartite ferromagnetic spin network with three independently thermalized sites. The theorem gives a complete nonlinear effective conductance law, a model-independent ordering of hot/cold bath currents within the specified model, a unique intermediate-reservoir balance temperature, strict entropy-production positivity, and a globally sharp orientation-only rectification ceiling. The results resolve an entire natural three-bath parameter space rather than a chosen numerical instance, and distinguish non-bipartite loop transport from open-trimer transport. There is no claim of large-system significance or phase transition.
